verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser's HyperAgent exposes a `page.ai()` primitive that takes natural-language descriptions of actions (e.g. 'search for flights... select the cheapest option') rather than brittle CSS selectors, and `page.extract()` pulls structured data via natural-language/schema description — both are DOM-understanding, selector-resilient action primitives as described in the story. However, the docs only show this single high-level natural-language action call rather than discrete named click/type/act primitives, and there is no independent or hands-on evidence confirming resilience specifically across selector/layout changes. Missing for 10: granular primitive-level documentation (explicit click/type/act functions), independent verification that actions survive DOM/layout changes over time.
